comment: All bands, materials, cables, parts, KPI presets and report colors are data. Phase 2 (LMR/FirstNet) and phase 3 (5G NR) add entries here without code changes. Phase 4 (Class 1 labor estimates) lives in config/estimating.json (factor values, rate card) + config/labor_units.json (catalog, regenerate with scripts/build_labor_units.py). Frequencies are DL center MHz (arithmetic midpoint of the DL block). NR bands carry technology=5G NR which opts them into the kpi_presets.nr_ssrsp SS-RSRP evaluation. Wall losses are dB at wall_loss_ref_mhz, scaled linearly in the log-frequency domain (ITU-R P.2040-style). Cable loss is dB/100m at anchor GHz values, interpolated linearly in the log-frequency domain. Per-band low-band overrides: n_exponent_overrides (per-environment N for this band) and wall_loss_scale_db (additive dB correction on every scaled wall loss). Optional per-band ss_rsrp_offset_db converts composite carrier RSSI to SS-RSRP estimate (total_port_EIRP - 10log10(N_RE) style; leave unset for 0). More NR bands are config-only additions, e.g. the 3.3 GHz n78 (3300-3800 MHz, DL midpoint 3550 in Europe, or a 3.3-3.4 GHz block at 3350): copy an N77_CBAND entry and set id/label/freq_mhz - no code changes needed.
p1238_validity_note: ITU-R P.1238 (editions 10+) applies indoors from 300 MHz up to 100 GHz; the tool window here is 300-6000 MHz to cover the NR n77 C-band presets. VHF 150 (and to a lesser extent UHF 450) still sits below the window: N and wall losses are extrapolated, so predict() emits a model_warning and per-band n_exponent_overrides / wall_loss_scale_db exist to calibrate. Editable.
building_types_note: Default indoor propagation per building type, used ONLY when a floor has no walls drawn (floor.building_type, else project building_type). PL = 20log10(f) + N*log10(d) + clutter_db_per_m*d - 28 (+ floor loss). Walls drawn -> the project environment N plus wall crossings, exactly as before. Each value carries a grade: P = published value (n_ref names the source), E = estimate with no published coefficient (analog noted, calibrate against closed jobs before relying on it). N values are the ~2 GHz column; use a band's n_exponent_overrides[<building_type id>] to set a different N for a band. clutter_db_per_m is an optional extra loss per metre (obstruction/clutter loss): calibrated values are grade C (see clutter_ref), others are estimates (grade E) or 0.0. Cross-check literature (not used for numbers here): COST 231 one-slope / multi-wall models (COST 231 Final Report, Digital Mobile Radio Towards Future Generation Systems, 1999), which express the same distance-slope idea. The ITU-R P.1238 Table 2 values below match the environments block above; re-check them against the edition you cite before issuing a design.
building_types_subtype_note: office is the generic type, used when the layout is unknown. office_open (open plan, atria, halls), office_standard (standard corporate) and office_dense (dense private offices, cubes, labs) take office N and differ only in clutter. office_open and office_dense clutter are grade E starting values from clutter_map classes, not calibrated.
system_type_note: Optional system_type (project, floor or autoplace request; the request wins, then floor, then project) selects clutter_by_system[<system>] on a building type when it has one, instead of clutter_db_per_m. No building type carries clutter_by_system yet, so the setting changes nothing until calibration adds values. clutter_by_system_grade and clutter_by_system_ref are per building type.

clutter_map_note: Per-square clutter classes scored from a floor plan image (romtool/clutter_map.py; README section 'Clutter map'). When a floor carries a clutter map and has no walls drawn, predict and autoplace replace the uniform building-type clutter term with the sum over squares of db_per_m x path length through the square along the straight antenna-to-point line; the building type (or environment) N still sets the distance term. Walls drawn take precedence exactly as before (the map is then ignored). Every number in this block is grade E (estimate): the class dB/m values are STARTING values derived from the calibrated building-type clutter (office 0.3, hospital 0.6, warehouse_open 1.0; grade C in building_types) and have not been calibrated per class. The scoring thresholds are tuning values chosen on synthetic plans, not measured on ANS plans. Calibrate classes against closed jobs before relying on counts.

clutter_map.param_ref: estimate: cell_m 3 m is the default square from the request; dark_threshold is mid-gray; min_wall_len_m (shortest straight dark run kept as wall, drops text and hatching), smooth_cells (window radius in squares), core_fill_pct (ink fraction that marks solid core poche), light_cpm / dense_cpm (wall crossings per metre, mean of both axes, bounding open / light / dense) and exterior_max_dark_pct are tuning values with no published source
clutter_map.zones_note: Zones (romtool/zones.py; README section 'Area zones') use the classes below. Classes with a calibrated building type value take that value and grade (C). Other zone values are starting values, grade E, with the source named in ref. height_band and pathway are the class defaults for a zone's ceiling height and cable pathway (names from ceiling_height_bands and cable_pathways). Codes must be unique one-character keys; '_' is reserved for the zones-only fallback square.

perimeter.ref: estimate: no published figure for any value. Starting values were set by hand on synthetic plans (tests/test_perimeter.py) and checked on one real office plan (page 1 of a customer RFQ set, 36 x 24 in vector PDF); they are not calibrated across plans. dark_threshold 128 is mid-gray; work_max_side 800 bounds the work grid; ink_fraction 0.1 counts a work cell as ink when 10 percent of its pixels are dark (thin CAD hairlines survive the downsample); min_feature_m 0.6 drops text glyphs and ticks; frame_frac 0.85 drops a sheet border spanning the page; frame_min_span 0.5 is the smallest span (both directions) of a closed ring that may be a sheet frame; frame_margin_frac 0.03 of the short side (and at least 2 gap distances) is the blank margin tested just inside the ring; frame_blank_frac 0.5 is the share of the ring that must have that margin blank. Lowered from 0.75 after the Burnett sheet measured 0.58: the building sits inside the margin along the east and west sides of the frame. A building's own exterior ring fails far below 0.5 because rooms and furniture stand against its walls; frame_peel_max 3 caps the peel rounds (0 turns peeling off); roi_line_m 0.2 is the widest line removed along a box edge (roi_line_px 3 without a scale); roi_edge_m 1.0 is how far from the edge such a line may lie (roi_edge_px 8 without a scale); roi_edge_share 0.4 is the share of the edge length the line must cover. Ink within roi_edge_m of a box edge that is continuous along roi_edge_share of the edge (gaps of at most roi_border_gap_m 0.3 m, roi_border_gap_px 6 without a scale) is treated as sheet border and removed whatever its thickness; a column pattern with regular gaps is kept. Limit: a solid wall within roi_edge_m of a box edge is removed with it, so draw the box at least roi_edge_m outside the walls; These cut sheet-border lines inside the box and keep thick walls. roi_cut_min_px 2 is the number of pixels where ink crosses a box edge (dark one pixel inside and one outside) before the box is reported as cutting the building; gap_m 1.0 closes door and window gaps up to about 2 m wide; gap_frac_unknown 0.03 is the pixel fallback (share of the short side, about one 0.9 m door at a 30 m plan width) when the scale is unknown; keep_regions 1 and region_min_frac 0.05 choose the building among separate footprints; max_footprint_frac 0.9 rejects a trace that leaked to most of the page; simplify_m 0.3 is the Douglas-Peucker tolerance; snap_deg 3 straightens near-axis edges.

autoplace_note: Defaults for POST /projects/{pid}/floors/{fid}/autoplace. Engineering values here are grade E (estimates, not measured or published): slack_m_per_run, donor feeder length, floor_height_m, max_plan_points, plan_margin_pct. public_safety_band_ids select the bands that get the NFPA two-tier rule instead of the single threshold.

autoplace.tap_min_gain_ref: estimate: hysteresis for choosing a tap/coupler stage over equal splitters, so a device is used only when it lowers the worst per-antenna device loss (or the spread) by at least this much; tuning value, not a published figure
autoplace.max_remotes_ref: estimate: search ceiling for the remote-unit count sizer, not an engineering limit; raise it for very large floors

bands.label: 700 MHz Public Safety LMR (P25, 769-775 base TX)
800 MHz Public Safety LMR (P25, 851-869 base TX)

fiber_sm.label: Fiber, single-mode (head end to remote)
fiber_sm.loss_note: Optical fiber is not part of the RF cascade: the RF loss anchors are 0 on purpose. The link is modeled by the remote element (dl_gain_db, max_dl_out_dbm). Only the footage is carried (BOM). Optical loss budget and link margin are not checked.

cable_low_freq_note: Anchors start at 0.7 GHz; below that the 0.7 GHz value is clamped (conservative for VHF 150 / UHF 450 - real low-band loss is lower). Upper anchors 3.0/4.0 GHz added in phase 3 so n41 (2.6 GHz) and n77 C-band (3.8 GHz) cascade runs interpolate instead of clamping at the 2.0 GHz anchor; values are representative, edit per cable datasheet.
branch_hardware_note: Fixed loss between the end of the last cable run and the antenna port: connectors, a jumper and, where several bands share one antenna, a diplexer/combiner. The allowance per antenna branch = connectors*connector.loss_db + jumpers*jumper.loss_db + diplexers*diplexer.loss_db (dB) and is applied in the cascade to every auto antenna when the autoplace request sets branch_losses. Every number below is grade E (estimate): none is taken from a datasheet or a published source; replace with the selected product's insertion loss. connector.per_branch counts individual connectors (a jumper has two ends). diplexer.per_branch applies only when the request covers more than diplexer.when_bands_gt bands.

connector.label: Connector (mated), each
connector.ref: estimate: representative mated-connector loss; no published value or datasheet cited

jumper.label: Jumper cable, each
jumper.ref: estimate: short flexible jumper at the antenna; replace with the cable datasheet at the band frequency and length

diplexer.label: Diplexer / combiner, each
diplexer.ref: estimate: representative diplexer insertion loss; replace with the selected OEM part

builders_note: Quantity rules for the assembly builders (romtool/builders.py, POST /projects/{pid}/builders/{name}). Every rule is {value, grade, ref}: grade C is a calibrated or ANS standard value with its reference named, grade E is an estimate. Change a value here, not in code. Floor height, riser slack and the power sizing inputs are read from autoplace, rflink and estimating config so each number has one home.

remote_note: Remote unit: an active element fed from the head end (repeater or source) by a fiber run, with its own downlink output cap per band. Modeled like the repeater: out = min(in + dl_gain_db, max_dl_out_dbm), per-band cap via max_dl_out_dbm_per_band. Every value below is grade E (no published figure, no vendor datasheet loaded): replace with the selected OEM remote spec. dl_gain_db 0 means the fiber link is level-neutral (the head-end port power is passed through, then capped); optical splitting and fiber loss are not modeled. Each band is capped independently (composite power sharing across bands is not modeled).

remote.label: Remote unit (fiber-fed active DAS)
remote.dl_gain_ref: fitted 2026-11-11 (run 5) together with the building-type clutter values on 32 ANS designs; a stand-in until the selected OEM remote spec is loaded, then refit clutter
remote.max_dl_out_ref: fitted 2026-11-11 (run 5) together with the building-type clutter values on 32 ANS designs; a stand-in for the selected OEM remote output per band, then refit clutter
remote.ports_ref: estimate: one RF output feeding the zone distribution tree

source.label: Off-air source (donor)
source.feeder_note: feeder_loss_db is an optional extra inline loss (e.g. donor-side jumper). The donor feeder run itself is modeled as an explicit cable_run element from source to repeater so it lands in the BOM.

direct.label: Direct inject (base station / P25 source feed)

kpi_thresholds_dbm_note: Coverage threshold(s); presets define required % of floor grid area at/above threshold. Tier scope: tier 1 always evaluates the whole floor; tier 2 evaluates inside critical-area polygons when any exist (else whole floor, with a note). 'scope' on a tier entry overrides the default. Bands whose technology matches nr_ssrsp.technology also get the SS-RSRP preset evaluated (whole floor), on the band's composite RSSI optionally shifted by a per-band ss_rsrp_offset_db.

nr_ssrsp.name: 5G NR SS-RSRP
nr_ssrsp.rsrp_class_note: Planning buckets (editable, % of floor area per class). 'none' = below the lowest class; classes are evaluated on the SS-RSRP estimate (composite RSSI + band ss_rsrp_offset_db).
